question: The classic opioid toxidrome consists of the triad: miosis (pinpoint pupils), respiratory depression, and altered consciousness (coma).

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The opioid triad (miosis + respiratory depression + coma) is the classic forensic and clinical recognition pattern. Exception: pethidine (meperidine) overdose can cause mydriasis due to its anticholinergic property — a worth-remembering variant.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The opioid triad — pinpoint pupils (miosis from central parasympathetic activation), respiratory depression (mu-receptor effect on brainstem respiratory centres), and coma — is the key diagnostic pattern. All three features are reversible with naloxone.
